question: If the heights of two cones are in the ratio 11 : 9 and their diameters are in the ratio 6 : 11, what is the ratio of their volumes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **heights** (h₁ : h₂) = 11 : 9

Ratio of **diameters** is 6 : 11, which is also the ratio of their **radii** (r₁ : r₂) = 6 : 11

Volume ratio V₁ : V₂ = (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂) = (6/11)² × (11/9) = (36/121) × (11/9) = 4 : 11

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of heights, h₁ : h₂ = 11 : 9

Ratio of diameters, d₁ : d₂ = 6 : 11

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone, V = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Since the ratio of diameters is equal to the ratio of radii, r₁ : r₂ = 6 : 11

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/adcaf235036e5cfa7bb33a390b5682746777772d945ce84257b9c2e6913e86ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let h₁ = 11h and h₂ = 9h

⇒ Let r₁ = 6r and r₂ = 11r

⇒ V₁/V₂ = [ (1/3) × π × r₁² × h₁ ] ÷ [ (1/3) × π × r₂² × h₂ ]

⇒ V₁/V₂ = (r₁² × h₁) ÷ (r₂² × h₂)

⇒ V₁/V₂ = (6² × 11) ÷ (11² × 9)

⇒ V₁/V₂ = (36 × 11) ÷ (121 × 9)

⇒ V₁/V₂ = 4/11

**∴ The correct answer is 4 : 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

The volume of a cone is given by the formula V = (1/3) × π × r² × h, where r is the radius of the circular base and h is the height.

Ratio relations for Cylindrical and Conical shapes

When comparing volumes, the ratio of the volumes of two cones or cylinders depends quadratically on their radii ratio and linearly on their height ratio.</p
